title: When Students Help Make the Rules
title_ja: 生徒が校則づくりに参加するとき

source_links.title: UNICEF: Convention on the Rights of the Child, Article 12

fact_notes: 児童の意見表明と考慮についての権利は条約第12条を参照。学校の会議例は架空であり、特定学校の制度を描写しない。
本文・和訳・設問はオリジナル。

sentences.en: A junior high school plans to change its rules about using the library during lunch.
sentences.ja: ある中学校が昼休みの図書館利用規則を変更する計画を立てます。

sentences.en: Teachers want to reduce noise, but students say the library is one of the few quiet places available.
sentences.ja: 教師は騒音を減らしたい一方、生徒たちは図書館は利用できる数少ない静かな場所の一つだと言います。

sentences.en: At first, the school leaders decide to write the new rule without asking students for their views.
sentences.ja: 最初、学校の管理職は生徒の意見を聞かずに新しい規則を書くことにします。

sentences.en: However, one teacher suggests holding a meeting where students can explain how the rule affects them.
sentences.ja: しかし、ある教師は規則が自分たちにどう影響するか生徒が説明できる会議を開くことを提案します。

sentences.en: The idea is not to let students make every decision, but to hear the people who will live with the result.
sentences.ja: 目的は生徒にすべての決定を任せることではなく、その結果に従う人々の声を聞くことです。

sentences.en: The Convention on the Rights of the Child recognizes children's right to express views in matters affecting them.
sentences.ja: 子どもの権利条約は、自分に関係する事柄について子どもが意見を表明する権利を認めています。

sentences.en: It also says those views should receive appropriate consideration according to age and maturity.
sentences.ja: その意見は年齢と成熟度に応じて適切に考慮されるべきだとも定めています。

sentences.en: For example, asking students about lunchtime noise can provide information adults might have missed.
sentences.ja: 例えば、昼休みの騒音について尋ねれば、大人が見落としていた情報が得られるかもしれません。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, listening to students does not mean that every suggestion must be accepted.
sentences.ja: それでも、生徒の意見を聞くことは、すべての提案を受け入れなければならないという意味ではありません。

sentences.en: The school still has a duty to protect safety and consider the needs of everyone.
sentences.ja: 学校には安全を守り、全員の必要を考える責任もあります。

sentences.en: At the meeting, some students ask for a quiet reading area, while others want space for small-group projects.
sentences.ja: 会議では静かな読書場所を求める生徒もいれば、小グループ活動の場所を求める生徒もいます。

sentences.en: A student representative suggests testing two different areas during a short trial period.
sentences.ja: 生徒代表は短い試行期間中、二つの異なる区域を試すことを提案します。

sentences.en: Instead of choosing only one group's preference, the participants explore whether both activities can share the library.
sentences.ja: 一つのグループの希望だけを選ぶのではなく、両方の活動が図書館を共有できるか検討します。

sentences.en: The librarian explains limits on staff time and the need to keep emergency exits clear.
sentences.ja: 司書は勤務時間の制約や非常口を空けておく必要を説明します。

sentences.en: These practical details help everyone understand why a good idea may still need adjustment.
sentences.ja: こうした実際的な事情によって、よい考えでも調整が必要な理由を全員が理解します。

sentences.en: After two weeks, the school collects feedback about noise, access, and student satisfaction.
sentences.ja: 2週間後、学校は騒音、利用しやすさ、生徒の満足度について意見を集めます。

sentences.en: Some students are pleased with the trial, while others suggest small changes to the signs and seating.
sentences.ja: 試行に満足する生徒もいれば、表示や座席の小さな変更を提案する生徒もいます。

sentences.en: The school does not promise to satisfy every person, but it explains the reasons for its final decision.
sentences.ja: 学校は全員を満足させるとは約束せず、最終決定の理由を説明します。

sentences.en: As a result, the process becomes easier to understand even for people who preferred another plan.
sentences.ja: その結果、別の案を望んでいた人にとっても、過程が理解しやすくなります。

sentences.en: Fair participation involves opportunities to speak and clear explanations of how ideas were considered.
sentences.ja: 公正な参加には、発言の機会と意見がどう考慮されたかの明確な説明が含まれます。

sentences.en: The final rule separates quiet reading from group work and promises a review at the end of the term.
sentences.ja: 最終的な規則は静かな読書とグループ活動を分け、学期末の見直しを約束します。

sentences.en: Not everyone considers it perfect, yet more students understand the reasons behind the decision.
sentences.ja: 全員が完璧だと考えてはいませんが、より多くの生徒が決定の理由を理解しています。

sentences.en: Therefore, the meeting has taught both students and teachers something about shared responsibility.
sentences.ja: そのため、この会議は生徒と教師の双方に共同の責任について教えました。

sentences.en: Students discover that having a voice includes listening to other people's needs and limits.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは意見を持つことには、他者の必要や制約に耳を傾けることも含まれると知ります。

sentences.en: A rule can become more trustworthy when those affected can understand how it was made.
sentences.ja: 規則は、影響を受ける人々がその作られ方を理解できるとき、より信頼されるものになり得ます。

questions.prompt: Why do some students object to new library restrictions?
options: The library is one of their few quiet spaces.
The school has closed permanently.
They want every room to become a gym.
They never use the library.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の「教師は騒音を減らしたい一方、生徒たちは図書館は利用できる数少ない静かな場所の一つだと言います。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of asking students for opinions?
options: To give students all legal authority.
To avoid protecting safety.
To cancel every school rule.
To hear how the rule affects people who use the library.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の「目的は生徒にすべての決定を任せることではなく、その結果に従う人々の声を聞くことです。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Which right is described in the convention?
options: Every student controls the school budget.
Adults may never make school decisions.
Children can express views about matters affecting them.
Children can refuse every school lesson.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「子どもの権利条約は、自分に関係する事柄について子どもが意見を表明する権利を認めています。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Does listening require accepting every student suggestion?
options: No, because children have no views.
No, the school must still consider safety and other needs.
Yes, every suggestion must become a rule.
Yes, if the student speaks loudly.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「それでも、生徒の意見を聞くことは、すべての提案を受け入れなければならないという意味ではありません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is the student representative's suggestion?
options: Try two different areas for a short period.
Close the library during lunch.
Replace all books with computers.
Use the same seats for every activity.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「生徒代表は短い試行期間中、二つの異なる区域を試すことを提案します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why does the librarian discuss staffing and exits?
options: A librarian can ignore all safety needs.
All students want the library closed.
Staff time has no effect on services.
Practical limits can affect whether a plan works.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「こうした実際的な事情によって、よい考えでも調整が必要な理由を全員が理解します。」が根拠です。

options: All students are given new phones.
The rule is forgotten.
The school collects feedback about the trial.
The library becomes a restaurant.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「2週間後、学校は騒音、利用しやすさ、生徒の満足度について意見を集めます。」が根拠です。

options: Accepting only popular opinions.
Chances to speak and explanations of how ideas were used.
Only allowing one student to speak.
Keeping all reasons secret.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「公正な参加には、発言の機会と意見がどう考慮されたかの明確な説明が含まれます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How do students respond to the final rule?
options: Not all like it, but more understand its reasons.
All students consider it perfect.
Every student refuses to use the library.
No one learns anything from the process.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落の「全員が完璧だと考えてはいませんが、より多くの生徒が決定の理由を理解しています。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Fair rules never need explanation.
Students should always make decisions alone.
Listening to different views is a waste of time.
Clear, inclusive rule-making can support shared responsibility.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落の「規則は、影響を受ける人々がその作られ方を理解できるとき、より信頼されるものになり得ます。」が根拠です。

grammar.focus: where students can explain how the rule affects them
grammar.explanation_ja: where節がmeetingを修飾し、how節が説明内容を表します。

grammar.focus: does not mean that every suggestion must be accepted
grammar.explanation_ja: that節がmeanの内容を表し、受動態が含まれます。

grammar.focus: Instead of choosing only one group's preference
grammar.explanation_ja: instead of + 動名詞は『一つの希望だけを選ぶ代わりに』です。

grammar.focus: when those affected can understand how it was made
grammar.explanation_ja: when節が信頼を得やすい条件を示します。

discourse.role_ja: 逆接：管理職だけで決める案から意見を聞く案へ進みます。
例示：大人の見落としを防ぐ生徒の意見です。
帰結：説明を受けることで過程が理解しやすくなります。
帰結：会議から共同責任の学びにつながります。

paraphrases.source: The idea is not to let students make every decision, but to hear the people who will live with the result.
paraphrases.rewrite: The goal is to hear those affected, not to give students every decision.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 当事者の声を聞くことと全決定権を区別します。

paraphrases.source: Nevertheless, listening to students does not mean that every suggestion must be accepted.
paraphrases.rewrite: Taking students seriously does not require approving every proposal.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 尊重と全面採用は別だという意味です。

paraphrases.source: Fair participation involves opportunities to speak and clear explanations of how ideas were considered.
paraphrases.rewrite: Fair processes provide chances to speak and explain how feedback matters.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 参加と説明の要素をまとめています。

paraphrases.source: A rule can become more trustworthy when those affected can understand how it was made.
paraphrases.rewrite: Rules gain credibility when affected people understand their development.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 作られ方の理解が信頼を高めるという結論です。
